{{Quote|Nida, my daughter, you're more than the only good thing to come from Seelah. You're the future of the Sith on this planet. It wasn't&hellip; our choice to live here. But it is&hellip; our choice not to die here. That choice&hellip; will be made by you&hellip;|Yaru Korsin's final words|<ref name="pantheon">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Pantheon]]''</ref>}}
'''Nida Korsin''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|female]] member of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Kesh/Legends|Kesh's]] [[Lost Tribe of Sith]] who eventually became [[Grand Lord]] of the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] order. Korsin was [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] the daughter of Grand [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Yaru Korsin]] and his [[Marriage/Legends|wife]], [[Seelah Korsin|Seelah]], and was delivered into a unique [[Korsin family|family]] dynamic&mdash;Yaru had [[Duel near the Omen|killed]] Seelah's [[Devore Korsin|previous husband]] several [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before Korsin's birth, and Seelah [[Marriage/Legends|married]] him in an effort to secure the futures of herself and her [[Jariad Korsin|son]], all while planning Yaru's downfall. While Seelah tried to suppress Korsin's [[Sith training|training]] in the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] ways, Korsin secretly learned the dark side through subterfuge by her [[Parent/Legends|father]] and was groomed to eventually succeed him. An avid [[uvak]]-rider, she was placed in charge of the [[Skyborn Rangers]] riding club, which also served as a military force in preparation for an anticipated armed uprising by Seelah and her son, Jariad. 

In [[4975 BBY]], that finally came to pass. Although Yaru was [[Death/Legends|fatally]] wounded in the [[Duel near the Kesh Sith Temple|battle]], Korsin and her Skyborn Rangers turned the tide and crushed the coup attempt. Korsin subsequently became the new Grand Lord, ushering in an unprecedented golden age for the Lost Tribe. She died heirless in the year [[4896 BBY]], after a seventy-nine-year reign, her passing ending the dynastic system of succession in the Lost Tribe.

==Biography==
===Secret training===
{{Quote|She's the daughter of the Grand Lord. What must the ''Keshiri'' think?|Seelah Korsin's reaction to Nida Korsin's entrance with the Skyborn Rangers at a festival|<ref name="savior" />}}
[[File:Yaru_Korsin.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Yaru Korsin, Nida Korsin's father.]]
A [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|female]], Nida Korsin was [[Reproduction/Legends|born]]<ref name="paragon" /> around [[4995 BBY]],<ref name="Birth date" /> the daughter of [[Yaru Korsin|Yaru]] and [[Seelah Korsin]], on the remote [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Kesh/Legends|Kesh]].<ref name="paragon" /> Both of Korsin's [[Parent/Legends|parents]] were members of the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] organization known as the [[Lost Tribe of Sith]]&mdash;comprised of survivors of the crashed [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith]] [[Sith dreadnaught|starship]] ''[[Omen]]''&mdash;of which Korsin's father, once [[Captain/Legends|captain]] of the ''Omen'', was named [[Grand Lord]]. Seelah was originally [[Marriage/Legends|married]] to Yaru's half-brother, [[Devore Korsin|Devore]], who survived the crash of the ''Omen'' along with Korsin's parents, only to [[Duel near the Omen|die]] at Yaru's hand after an attempt to seize power.<ref name="savior" /> 

In an effort to ensure the positions of herself and her son, [[Jariad Korsin|Jariad]], Seelah married her husband's [[Death/Legends|killer]] and bore Nida, all while planning Yaru's downfall.<ref name="paragon" /> Although Korsin was Seelah's only daughter, Korsin's mother only saw her as a genealogical detail and actively tried to restrict Korsin's [[Sith training|training]] in the Sith ways, while grooming Jariad as the future Grand [[Lord/Legends|Lord]].<ref name="savior" />

In what was ostensibly a gesture of Sith trust in the [[Keshiri/Legends|Keshiri]] natives, the young Nida Korsin was boarded in one village after another with a series of Keshiri [[Nurse/Legends|nurse]]-maids and tutors, preventing her from receiving anything more than rudimentary training in the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]]. However, Yaru found a way around Seelah's machinations. The Grand Lord staged the deaths of several loyal subordinates who taught Korsin in secret during the night. During the [[Standard day/Legends|day]], Korsin, who became an able rider of the avian [[uvak]] beasts indigenous to Kesh, served as an aerial [[Ambassador/Legends|ambassador]] amongst the Keshiri, giving her an opportunity to win friends among the natives and build a network of informants. Secretly, she was being groomed to eventually take control of the Lost Tribe, all right under her mother's [[Nose/Legends|nose]].<ref name="savior" />

===Leader of the Skyborn Rangers===
{{Quote|Father tried to throw him over the side with the Force. He tried&hellip;and when he failed, I did it.|Nida to Seelah, on her father Yaru and her brother Jariad|<ref name="savior" />}}
In [[4975 BBY]], for Korsin's twentieth [[Birthday/Legends|birthday]], she was placed in charge of an uvak-riding club known as the [[Skyborn Rangers]]. Although they appeared to be nothing more than a group of hobby-riders, the Skyborn Rangers were all trained Sith warriors and were secretly prepared to defend Grand Lord Yaru in case of an anticipated armed uprising by Seelah and Jariad. Although over the last twenty-five [[Standard year/Legends|years]] the Lost Tribe had made efforts to find a way off Kesh, by then they had given up and committed to live amongst the Keshiri for good. Their intentions were declared in a massive celebration in the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Tahv]], featuring a grand entrance on uvak-back by Korsin and her Rangers, which was met with a mixed reception.<ref name="savior" />

[[File:Uvak.jpg|thumb|left|250px|An uvak beast, of which Nida Korsin was an avid rider]]
In her capacity as head of the Skyborn Rangers, Korsin became close with the group's traveling stable master, [[Tona Vaal]], son of [[Korsin family]] friend [[Adari Vaal]]. As Korsin would soon learn, Vaal was member of a [[Keshiri resistance]] group led by his mother that was ready to [[Keshiri uprising in Keshtah|strike and carry out their plan]] to overthrow Sith rule. Their plan involved the theft of thousands of uvak vital to Sith control, which would be sent to their deaths to set up an armed uprising. However, Vaal fell for Korsin and divulged the details of the plot to her, allowing her to prevent most of the uvak from being stolen.<ref name="savior" />

At the same [[Time/Legends|time]], she and her Skyborn Rangers were called in for their main purpose. After thwarting the resistance's efforts, Korsin rushed to the [[Kesh Sith Temple]] with her compatriots on uvak-back&mdash;Seelah and Jariad had [[Duel near the Kesh Sith Temple|attacked]]. Although Yaru valiantly fought back, by the time Korsin arrived her father was wounded and cornered. Igniting her [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]], Korsin jumped into the fray, and she and her Rangers turned the tide of the battle. In a final stand, Yaru tried to throw Jariad off a precipice, but when he failed, Korsin did it for him, killing her brother. Seelah was wounded and knocked [[Sleep/Legends|unconscious]] in an explosion, and lost the use of her [[Limb/Legends|legs]]. In his last act, Yaru commended his legacy to Korsin, a change ratified by the three surviving Sith [[High Lord]]s, officially making her the new Grand Lord.<ref name="savior" />

===Grand Lord===
{{Quote|I came here because we just had the reading of Father's final testament. He commends his legacy to me&mdash;and the three surviving High Lords have ratified it. So you see? You ''are'' the mother of the new Grand Lord. Congratulations.|Nida Korsin, to Seelah Korsin, after the latter's wounding|<ref name="savior" />}}
[[File:KeshSithTemple.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Kesh Sith Temple]]
In the first [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]] of her Grand Lordship, Korsin made several declarations in accordance with her father's final wishes: henceforth, although not including Seelah, the spouse and household laborers of the Grand Lord would be executed upon the ruler's death. In Seelah's case, Korsin ordered for the immediate withdrawal of the Sith from the Temple, leaving her mother there to live out the rest of her days alone. When Seelah awoke hours after the battle's end, Korsin was at her side and broke the news.<ref name="savior" />

Korsin received another gift from her father&mdash;a map of a previously unknown [[Alanciar|continent]] far across the [[Ocean/Legends|sea]], discovered from examination of the last visual data taken by the ''Omen'' twenty-five years prior. Knowing that the continent was inhabited, Korsin was sworn to keep its existence a secret, only to be revealed when the people truly needed to know.<ref name="secrets">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Secrets]]''</ref> She went on to have a celebrated reign as Grand Lord, initiating a golden age for the Lost Tribe. She eventually married a [[Nida Korsin's consort|man]] who became her [[Grand Consort|Lord Consort]],<ref name="purgatory" />  and in [[4960 BBY]]<ref name="Farawaypress">{{Faraway|url=fiction/ebooks/sw-losttribeofthesith5.html|text=''Star Wars: Lost Tribe of the Sith Part 5: Purgatory''}}</ref> they had a son, [[Donellan]]. Although Donellan was in line to assume his mother's position, Korsin went on to outlive her son, who had waited too long to make his move. Heirless, she abolished the dynastic system, instead instituting succession based on merit.<ref name="purgatory" /> 

Korsin went on to reign for seventy-nine years&mdash;still regarded as a record as of [[3000 BBY]]<ref name="pantheon" />&mdash;and eventually died in [[4896 BBY]].<ref name="Death date" /> In honor of her reign, the [[Festival of Nida's Rise]], held every seventy-nine years, was instituted. By 3000 BBY, Korsin and her father were the most celebrated figures on Kesh, depicted in statues and monuments all over the land.<ref name="pantheon" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|You ''are'' a child.|Seelah Korsin, to Nida Korsin|<ref name="savior" />}}
Although she outwardly appeared to be harmless and even somewhat bumbling, Nida Korsin was secretly a cunning and capable leader of Sith. She was charismatic and active in her community as leader of the Skyborn Rangers. As her father, Yaru's, heir, Korsin was very loyal to the Grand Lord, coming to his rescue and saving him from Seelah's and Jariad's attack. Meanwhile, she reflected her mother's cold attitude toward herself, abandoning her to die alone in the isolated Kesh [[Sith temple/Legends|Sith Temple]]. Her face resembled her mother Seelah's and she had short-cropped [[Hair/Legends|hair]].<ref name="savior" />

==Powers and abilities==
{{Quote|Your son should be careful, Adari. He's been spending a lot of time with Nida. It's that Korsin charm that keeps you Vaals around.|Yaru Korsin to Adari Vaal, on Tona Vaal and Nida Korsin|<ref name="savior" />}}
Despite her mother's best efforts, Nida Korsin learned the dark side of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] in secret, eventually becoming adept in the ways of the Sith. In addition, she was extremely skilled with a lightsaber, [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|mowing down]] with ease Seelah's and Jariad's forces in the battle near the Kesh Sith Temple. She was a master manipulator and found it easy to win people over, earning her the allegiance of dozens of friends and informants&mdash;exemplified by her charming of Tona Vaal, who subsequently revealed the Keshiri resistance's hidden plans to her. Korsin was also a capable uvak rider, an ability she employed in her capacity with the Skyborn Rangers.<ref name="savior" /> After her father's death, she showed herself to be an excellent leader and [[Governor/Legends|governor]], bringing the Lost Tribe of Sith into an unparalleled golden age.<ref name="purgatory" />

==Equipment==
Korsin wielded a red lightsaber. As a uvak-rider, Korsin wore [[Clothing/Legends|clothes]] to represent herself as rugged and lively, which included a uvak-[[Leather/Legends|leather]] vest, chaps, and face paint. However, Seelah considered the outfit to be an abomination to fashion and thought it made Korsin look comical.<ref name="savior" />

==Behind the scenes==
Nida Korsin was first mentioned in ''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Paragon]]'', the third [[eBook]] in [[John Jackson Miller]]'s [[Star Wars: Lost Tribe of the Sith|''Lost Tribe of the Sith'']] series.<ref name="paragon" /> She made her first appearance in the series' next installment, [[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Savior|''Savior'']].<ref name="savior" />
